chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Administration confirmed climate change is factored into flood risk assessments.
This project marks the completion of the first phase of the flood control strategy.
Administration will report back this fall with options for the next flood control phase.

25.description: The Saskatoon Fire Department's 2025 review highlighted a 13.2% increase in calls, including a near doubling of overdose responses and significant encampment incidents, alongside major emergency coordination efforts.

chips.text: Chief Wegren stated all divisions want more resources but administration must be responsible.
Saskatoon hosted 8,000 northern Saskatchewan wildfire evacuees for 86 days.
The provincial EOC was activated for the first time in Saskatchewan's history.
Councillor Tino requested specific overdose data for downtown and Riversdale.
Encampment responses increased, highlighting risks of homelessness and addictions.
Chief Wegren committed to sharing specific overdose data for downtown and Riversdale.

17.description: Saskatoon is proactively strengthening its water distribution system, including pipe replacements and new infrastructure, after Calgary's 2024-2025 water main failures.

chips.text: City is planning a future water treatment plant on the east side of the river.

18.description: The city gathered extensive public and stakeholder feedback in 2024-2025 for a new Climate Action Strategy, aiming to reduce carbon pollution and prepare Saskatoon for climate change impacts, with a focus on equity.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Councillor asked how the strategy will shift climate burden from vulnerable populations.
Living Sky Wildlife Rehabilitation stressed the importance of biodiversity and ecosystems.
Strategy will embed equity, reconciliation, and prioritize vulnerable populations.
The full Climate Action Strategy is expected for Council approval in August.

22.description: Saskatoon is planning a multi-unit organics collection program for fall 2027, expanding services to 970 properties. Preliminary 2027 rates are estimated at $2.79 per unit per month.

chips.text: Expands organics collection to 970 multi-unit properties, affecting over 43,000 dwelling units.
Rates will be presented for approval during the 2027 budget review in November 2026.
